subject: Failback thresholds, maintenance window alignment, and rollback sim plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ops@acmehealth.com
Cc: sre-lead@orionbank.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Failback thresholds, maintenance window alignment, and rollback sim plan

Team / Acme ops —

Quick summary: we're going to run a maintenance window for Acme's private VPC deployment next Friday 2026-06-04 UTC 02:00-04:00 (PDT 19:00-21:00). The objective is a minor runtime upgrade (v2.11.3 -> v2.12.0) with minimal disruption and a validated rollback path.

Primary asks before EOD Monday:
- Confirm a single 2-hour window works for Acme (can be shifted +/- 2 hours).
- Sign off on failback thresholds (attached matrix) — we propose automatic failback if 4 consecutive 5m windows show: p50 latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate > 0.8% OR token throughput < 70% of baseline.
- Approve Canary scope: 5% traffic across two AZs with synthetic replay.

Notes on rollback model: we prefer a staged rollback (canary -> all) with an emergency hot rollback option that tears down the new runtime and re-pins nodes to v2.11.3. Rolling back will require: revoke new model variant pins, reapply cached KV snapshots, and a short rewarm period (estimated 4–6 minutes for heavy caches).

Attachments: failback threshold matrix, canary traffic playbook (short checklist).

I'll run a tabletop rollback sim on Wednesday with ops + SRE; can you indicate who from Acme will join?

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Failback thresholds, maintenance window alignment, and rollback sim plan

Rafael —

Agree with the window. A couple of clarifications on the threshold matrix:
- For the latency rule, make it p95 > 2x baseline instead of p50 > 1.5x. P50 can be noisy during canaries.
- Add a fidelity check for long-tail token completion (any truncation errors reported by the runtime).

Operational items I'll own for the sim:
- Produce a short runbook that lists the exact commands to re-pin and rehydrate KV caches (will attach draft Monday).
- Coordinate telemetry dashboards: I want a single view with p95/p99 latency, error-rate, CDN/egress throughput, and token throughput.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood

+1 to Laura's p95 suggestion. A few additional items from the runtime perspective:

- Canary composition: route read-only traffic + synthetic write-replay to canary. No live write mutations unless Acme explicitly approves (we should avoid billing-impacting state changes).
- KV snapshot cadence: take a consistency snapshot 30 minutes before the window, and upload to a customer-isolated bucket. Include an integrity hash so rollback can validate snapshots before rehydration.
- Circuit breaker: introduce a soft-circuit at 10% error-rate for canary; at 0% we immediately promote to all traffic — so we need manual gating.

I'll attach a short script to automate snapshot/hydration and an ops-checklist by Monday.

Karthik

Subject: Re: Failback thresholds, maintenance window alignment, and rollback sim plan

Thanks for the alignment. Answers inline: 

> 1) What is the expected client-side reconnect behavior if you perform a staged rollback? Any session tokens we should expect to refresh?

- For the short staged rollback we expect persistent connections to be dropped and clients to reconnect. Session tokens remain valid — we don't rotate any auth keys during this operation. Recommend clients back off with jitter (0.5s-3s) for reconnect attempts. We'll add a short advisory to Acme SDK docs.

> 2) If we trigger emergency hot rollback, will there be a brief period where requests will 502 because of mismatched KV state?

- Short answer: yes, a transient 502 window is possible during hot rollback while the runtime swaps binaries and rehydrates caches. Mitigations:
  - Use our prefix KVCaching so warm entries are re-used where possible.
  - Run a small traffic fan-in after rollback to validate de-dup and token alignment before opening full traffic.

Operational next steps (I will own):
- Draft a one-page client advisory (how reconnect behaves, expected transient errors, SDK suggestions).
- Lead the tabletop on Wednesday 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC (invite to follow).
- Add a test to the sim that intentionally creates a KV mismatch to validate detection and failback.

Soojin
